newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Spanish, Portuguese PMs to discuss euro currency.
newsitem.headline: Spanish, Portuguese PMs to discuss euro currency.

text.p: The prime ministers of Spain and Portugal will focus heavily on their countries' ambitions to join a single European currency in a two-day meeting in the Azores from Tuesday, officials say.

Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar and his Portuguese counterpart, Antonio Guterres, will also discuss other economic issues such as privatisation and steps to combat tax evasion, as well as the sensitive matter of sharing water resources.

"Economic and Monetary Union will be the centre of attention at the summit, because Portugal and Spain will want to reaffirm their desire to join the "hard core' of EMU," a senior Portuguese government source said.
"They will make a strong joint statement about their wish to be founder members of EMU," he added.

"Spain and Portugal have common objectives in terms of their ambition to join the single currency. Both countries want to join the first group and so they are bound to want to cooperate on this issue," a bank analyst said.
Spain and Portugal have frequently expressed their determination to be among the first wave of countries to join the single currency, or euro, in January 1999.
A much thornier issue to be tackled by the two leaders will be the sharing of scarce water resources.
The neighbours have had disputes over water in the past. All the major rivers flowing through Portugal rise in Spain.

Water levels in the Douro, Tagus and Guadiana rivers have fallen sharply over the last 20 years due in part to drought but also to the diversion of water into huge dams in Spain, Portuguese officials said.
As Spain struggles to provide its parched southern regions with water, Portugal claims it is not getting its fair share.
The Portuguese government source said Portugal had sent to Spain a discussion document on sharing water resources.
"Spain and Portugal have been coming closer together in their points of view on water recently," the source added.
The two countries also plan to discuss the war on terrorism and drug trafficking, Spanish and Portuguese officials said.

Portuguese Interior Minister Alberto Costa said this month that drug trafficking was the most serious crime threatening society and authorities were stepping up their watch over the coastline as a top priority.

The police forces of the two neighbouring countries are struggling to keep the pressure on increasingly innovative international drug gangs, which run heroin, cocaine and cannabis into the countries by land and sea.

Aznar and Guterres will also cover other international issues, such as ties with the Latin American Mercosur customs union, dialogue with Mediterranean nations and the peace process in the Middle East.
They will discuss the European Union's Dublin summit in December, the expansion of NATO and a meeting of the Organisation for Cooperation and Security in Europe (OSCE) in Lisbon on December 2-3.
